title: Power Platform: Dataverse audit events sent to Purview no longer carry before-and-after values
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap record and Microsoft documentation. The auditing controls and licensing statements check out, and the page correctly distinguishes Dataverse field values from the metadata still sent to Purview.

claims.where: front matter: status; What's changing; Scope; Why it matters
claims.claim: The roadmap item is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.where: front matter: releasePhase; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap targets June CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "June CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) is the only cloud listed in the roadmap record.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists the Web platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.where: front matter: products
claims.claim: The roadmap product is Microsoft Power Platform governance and administration.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Power Platform governance and administration"]

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The roadmap aims to prevent leaks of sensitive customer data, including financial, medical and personal information.
claims.quote: Examples of sensitive customer data include financial information, medical and health data, and personally identifiable information.

claims.where: What's changing; title; summary
claims.claim: Dataverse captures create and update events with before-and-after column values that remain in its audit logs rather than being sent to Purview.
claims.quote: In Dataverse audit logs, create and update events—including a column’s before-and-after values—are captured. These values remain in Dataverse audit logs, but aren’t sent to Purview activity logging.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The roadmap describes the removal as all customer data being removed from Purview-bound audit events.
claims.quote: all customer data is removed before these audit events are sent to Purview activity logging.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The roadmap's Enabled for line reads Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users.
claims.quote:
Enabled for:

Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Dataverse excludes before-and-after field change values from the audit events sent to Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Starting in May 2026, Dataverse will no longer include before-and-after field change values in the audit events that are sent to Microsoft Purview.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Audit events continue to flow to Purview after the field values are removed.
claims.quote: Audit events will continue to flow to Purview; however, the detailed field-level value changes will be excluded.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Purview continues receiving metadata identifying who made changes.
claims.quote: Purview continues receiving audit event metadata (such as who made changes, the date of the changes, and the tables affected), but field-level value changes will no longer be included.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Purview continues receiving the date of changes.
claims.quote: Purview continues receiving audit event metadata (such as who made changes, the date of the changes, and the tables affected), but field-level value changes will no longer be included.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Purview continues receiving metadata identifying the affected tables.
claims.quote: Purview continues receiving audit event metadata (such as who made changes, the date of the changes, and the tables affected), but field-level value changes will no longer be included.

claims.where: What's changing; summary; Risk assessment; controls[1]
claims.claim: Dataverse continues to store and expose before-and-after field changes through native audit APIs and tables.
claims.quote: Dataverse continues to store and expose before-and-after field changes through its native audit APIs and tables.

claims.where: What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The Learn notice gives a start of May 2026, different from the roadmap target.
claims.quote: Starting in May 2026, Dataverse will no longer include before-and-after field change values in the audit events that are sent to Microsoft Purview.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The removal is a platform change that takes effect without an administrator enabling it.
claims.quote: Starting in May 2026, Dataverse will no longer include before-and-after field change values in the audit events that are sent to Microsoft Purview.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Monitoring, alerting and reporting solutions dependent on Purview before-and-after values stop working when the removal takes effect.
claims.quote: If you have existing monitoring, alerting, or reporting solutions that depend on before-and-after field change values within Purview audit events, those solutions will stop working once this deprecation takes effect.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Microsoft names anomaly detection rules comparing old and new values as an affected example.
claims.quote: Rules that compare old/new values for anomaly detection.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft names pipelines analysing field-level deltas as an affected example.
claims.quote: Data pipelines that analyze field-level deltas.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft names custom compliance checks in Purview as an affected example.
claims.quote: Custom compliance checks running in Purview.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance; summary
claims.claim: Microsoft asks administrators to update affected monitoring and workflows to obtain field-level audit information directly from Dataverse.
claims.quote: Update your monitoring or downstream workflows to retrieve detailed field-level audit information directly from Dataverse, not from Purview.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft says no changes are required when Dataverse audit logs are the solution's source of truth.
claims.quote: No changes are required if your solution uses Dataverse audit logs as the source of truth.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Removing field values reduces sensitive-data exposure through downstream monitoring or analytics systems.
claims.quote: Removing detailed field-level values from Purview-bound audit events reduces the risk of exposing sensitive business or personal information through downstream monitoring or analytics systems.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Manage Dataverse auditing says columns with auditing turned off have before-and-after values sent to Purview as an asterisk.
claims.quote: When you turn off auditing for a column, the before-and-after values are sent as an "\*" to Microsoft Purview.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The activity logging page says column-level secured fields are sent to Purview with an asterisk.
claims.quote: Column-level secured fields are sent to Purview activity logging with an asterisk (\*).

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Viewing Audit Summary requires the View Audit Summary privilege.
claims.quote: Users need the **View Audit Summary** privilege to see the **Audit Summary** view.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Audit detail messages require the separate Dataverse privileges prvReadRecordAuditHistory and prvReadAuditSummary.
claims.quote: To use these messages, ensure you have the `prvReadRecordAuditHistory` and `prvReadAuditSummary` privileges.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope
claims.claim: Viewing Power Platform activity logs in Purview requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs.
claims.quote: To view Power Platform activity logs in Microsoft Purview, users need to be assigned either the **Audit Logs** or **View-Only Audit Logs** role.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope
claims.claim: Dataverse user access or activity logging is sent to Purview only for production environments.
claims.quote: User access or activity logging is sent to Purview for production environments only.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: System Administrator, System Customizer or equivalent permissions can configure Dataverse auditing.
claims.quote: You must have a system administrator or system customizer role or equivalent permissions to turn auditing on or off.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Environment auditing is controlled in Power Platform admin center at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Audit and logs > Audit settings > Global Audit Settings > Start Auditing.
claims.quote: Expand **Audit and logs** and then select **Audit settings**. ... Select **Global Audit Settings** to open the Microsoft Dynamics 365 system settings. From there, turn on **Start Auditing**

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The organizations PATCH endpoint at api/data/v9.2 changes environment auditing settings.
claims.quote: Change the column values in the organization table to change how auditing works for the environment. ... PATCH [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations([Organization ID]) HTTP/1.1

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The request-body property isauditenabled decides whether auditing is enabled for the environment.
claims.quote: | `IsAuditEnabled``isauditenabled`**Is Auditing Enabled** | Boolean | Whether auditing is enabled for the environment |

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Audit Summary is reached from a model-driven app at Settings > Advanced Settings > System > Auditing > Audit Summary view.
claims.quote: From the app, select the **Settings** icon on the banner, select **Advanced Settings**, and then select **System** > **Auditing** > **Audit Summary view**.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: GET api/data/v9.2/audits(<audit id>)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.RetrieveAuditDetails retrieves an audit event's details.
claims.quote: GET [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/audits(12869c65-d7d3-ec11-b656-281878f0eba9)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.RetrieveAuditDetails

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; controls[1]
claims.claim: Dataverse Audit History, Audit Summary and its API provide audit information for investigating previous field values.
claims.quote: You can view audit logs in the **Audit History** tab for a single record and in the **Audit Summary** view for all audited operations in a single environment. You can also retrieve audit logs by using the web API or the SDK for Microsoft .NET.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Dataverse stores audit logs in log storage capacity.
claims.quote: Dataverse stores audit logs and they consume log storage capacity.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model, licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The included licensing model is supported by Purview Audit (Standard) being included in all the Microsoft 365, Office 365 and Business plans enumerated in the briefing.
claims.quote:
| Feature | Microsoft 365 E3/A3/A1/G3/F3/F1 | Office 365 E3/E1/A3/A1/G3/G1/F3 | Microsoft 365 Business Basic/Standard/Premium |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Audit (Standard) | Included | Included | Included |

claims.where: front matter: previewDate
claims.claim: The roadmap provides no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The option to turn on audit logging is visible only when minimum Office licensing requirements are met.
claims.quote: The option to turn on audit logging is only visible when the minimum Office licensing requirements are met.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no licence or meter specific to the removal of Dataverse before-and-after values from Purview events.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse removal before after field change values Purview audit licensing price meter opt out disable May 2026; read the removal notice, activity logging prerequisites and Purview service description, including its Audit (Standard) table; none names a removal-specific licence or meter.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap description nor the Learn removal notice specifies a licence or meter for the change.
claims.quote: Searched: licence, licensing, price and meter in roadmap record 576863 and the entire removal-of-before-and-after-values section of Important changes coming in Power Platform; neither gives one.

claims.where: Scope
claims.claim: The Learn notice describes no opt-in or opt-out for the removal.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse removal before after field change values Purview audit licensing price meter opt out disable May 2026; read the full removal notice and activity logging prerequisites; the notice describes removal starting in May and downstream updates, not an opt-in or opt-out.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The existing Dataverse auditing and retrieval controls do not restore removed values to Purview, and the notice names no restoration step.
claims.quote: Update your monitoring or downstream workflows to retrieve detailed field-level audit information directly from Dataverse, not from Purview. Dataverse continues to store and expose before-and-after field changes through its native audit APIs and tables.

claims.where: Governance controls: Enable SAS Logging in Purview
claims.claim: Enable SAS Logging in Purview is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Privacy and Security > Storage Shared Access Signature (SAS) Security Settings > Enable SAS Logging in Purview.
claims.quote: Expand the **Product** list and select **Privacy and Security**. ... In the **Storage Shared Access Signature (SAS) Security Settings** section, toggle the **Enable SAS Logging in Purview** setting to **On**.

claims.where: Governance controls: Enable SAS Logging in Purview
claims.claim: Enable SAS Logging in Purview gives Purview access to production-environment activity logs rather than restoring the removed field values.
claims.quote: To give Microsoft Purview access to Power Platform environment data, turn on the **Enable SAS Logging in Purview** setting in the Power Platform admin center for each Power Platform production environment where you want to view audit logs in Microsoft Purview.

claims.where: Open questions
claims.claim: The published customer engagement apps schema describes Fields as containing created or updated values.
claims.quote: | `Fields` | Edm.String | No | JSON of Key Value pair reflecting the values that were created or updated |

claims.where: rationale: impact
claims.claim: The sources do not describe a change to maker or end-user workflows from the removal.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse removal before after field change values Purview audit; read roadmap 576863 and the complete Learn removal notice. The record's Enabled for line names end users, but the described impact is on Purview monitoring, alerting, reporting and downstream workflows.
